thread:
Ethan: heads-up — our nightly CI published a build log to a customer-facing GCS bucket. spotted a partial Vault token and a KMS resource name in the same line, redacting the token here. tagging sec-oncall.
Leila: oh no. which bucket? can you paste the line (remove token)?
Ethan: `2026-03-21T03:41:02Z build-123 INFO artifacts uploaded gs://partner-a-public/builds/123/logs.txt kms_key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/primary vault_token=VAULT.s.XXXX[REDACTED]`
Marco: immediate actions: 1) make bucket private 2) rotate any tokens that could be derived from that vault token 3) identify consumers of that KMS key.
sec-oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-042 created. severity: P2. runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/secrets-exposure. assigned: eng-security + infra.
Anna: Ethan — can you ACL the bucket now (gsutil acl set private ...) and snapshot the object for forensic copy to internal secure storage before any mutations?
Ethan: ACL set to private and object copied to gs://secure-incidents/INC-2026-042/logs-123.txt (immutably archived).
ci-bot: noticed failing pipeline job: `redact-logs` step error 403 after ACL change.
Leila: expected. We'll coordinate rollback if needed. Marco — can you create a short-lived policy to deny that pipeline SA from using the KMS key? We should avoid blanket revokes that break unrelated services.
Marco: creating IAM deny binding for serviceAccount:ci-pipeline@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com on `cryptoKeys/primary`. applying in prod+staging. ETA 7m.
Anna: While denies apply, we need to rotate Vault-side artifacts. Which token type was logged? Host token or accessor? If accessor, we can revoke by accessor.
Ethan: looks like a full token (starts with `VAULT.s.`) — I exported the accessor via vault token lookup using the copied log in secure storage and it shows `accessor: bX-abc`.
Leila: good catch. Revoke by accessor `vault token-revoke -accessor bX-abc`. Marco — once deny is in place, revoke.
Marco: revoked accessor and confirmed via `vault token-lookup` returning 403.
sec-oncall-bot: runbook step 2 complete: token revoked. next: KMS telemetry and rewrap.
Anna: For KMS, we should never re-encrypt by decrypting to plaintext locally. Use server-side rewrap: `gcloud kms keys versions rewrap --location=global --keyring=main --key=primary --ciphertext-file=old --ciphertext-file-out=new` or create new key and rewrap to it. Also enable audit logging for CMEK admin activity to SIEM.
Leila: proposal: create `primary-rot-2026-03-21` HSM-backed key with strict IAM (vault-service-sa + eng-security-rewrap role only). schedule canary rewrap on one artifact, validate consumers, then rewrap remainder.
Ethan: I'll prepare a list of artifacts referencing that key by searching Cloud Asset + build logs. Found 9 artifacts in last 7 days.
Marco: timeline: containment done. rotation window: 04:00-06:00 UTC. Rewrap canary at 04:10, rotate Vault secret versions at 04:25, monitor for 30m, widen.
Leila: also need CI changes: redact-logs step must scrub any pattern matching `VAULT.s.` and KMS resource ARNs before upload. Ethan — can you open a PR with the patch and add `--dry-run` to pipeline to ensure no regressions?
Ethan: PR opened: https://internal/pull/3456 patch adds jq filter and redact script. will add unit test.
Anna: post-rotation checklist: push CMEK and Vault rotation events to SIEM index `sec-ci-exposure-2026`, run an ownership sweep for long-lived CI tokens, and require partner to attest rotation if their bucket was public.
sec-oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-042 update: rewrap canary started at 04:10 UTC. monitor channel: #sec-telemetry.
Marco: I'll prepare rollback steps: rebind original key IAM if unexpected failures occur and restore object pointer to old ciphertext. documenting step-by-step in the incident ticket.
Leila: once everything is stable, schedule a retro to update CI artifact retention and add pre-upload validation.
Ethan: noted. will also add lint rule in pipeline: fail if `VAULT.s.` appears in artifacts. :white_check_mark:
Anna: good. thanks everyone. I'll follow up with SIEM parsers and close after postmortem.
sec-oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-042 severity remains P2. next update in 2h or on status change.
